clue.text: Mature insect a long way back in the past

indicators.note: back tells us to read the letters for a long way in the reverse direction

parts.note: MI is the abbreviation for a mile, a long way to walk
something in the past happened long ago

explanation.surface: A naturalist dates a full-grown insect to a period far back in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal; 'a long way' reads as distance but stands for the mile abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists use this term for the final, adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Demand is set to change in pub overlooking church

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of is set are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pub's demand for change is set, the building standing above the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' marks the anagram and 'in' the container; 'overlooking' works because in a down entry the pub stands above the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistence is a firm demand that something be done, a synonym in noun form.

clue.text: Luminous discharge seen this time of year?

indicators.note: seen points to a short word visible within the month, its outer letters set aside

parts.note: the time of year is taken as the spring month March

explanation.surface: Bright flashes are reported in the sky at this season.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is seen inside MARCH once its first and last letters, M and H, are dropped; the question mark admits the month is not printed.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric arc is a glowing discharge of current across a gap between electrodes.

clue.text: Experts know theirs to be specimens of Allium cepa

definitions.text: Experts know theirs to be specimens of Allium cepa

parts.words: Experts know theirs to be specimens of Allium cepa
parts.note: a play on the British idiom that an expert knows their stuff, here taken literally: Allium cepa is the botanical name of the common bulb vegetable

explanation.surface: Botanists are said to recognise their own specimens of a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'know your onions' is British slang for being expert in a subject; the clue takes the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Allium cepa is the Latin botanical name of the kitchen bulb, so specimens of it are these vegetables.

clue.text: Paint in bad state, being old

definitions.meaning: a water-based paint with glue or size, used on walls
in archaic use the word meant a disordered or ill-humoured condition of body or mind

explanation.surface: Paintwork has deteriorated badly because it is old.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a size-bound wall paint and, archaically, a disordered state or bad humour.

clue.text: To support wife, peer disposes of old farm building

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath, so the second piece goes below the wife

parts.note: DUTCH, from 'old Dutch', is Cockney slang for a wife

indicators.note: disposes of says a letter is thrown out of the word for a peer

parts.note: a baron is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman sells off an old building in order to provide for his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposes of' marks the deletion and 'To support' puts the building under the wife in this down entry. 'My old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is an open-sided farm structure with a curved roof for storing hay.

clue.text: Be vaguely aware of various points

definitions.meaning: to feel or detect something without clear evidence
a string of compass points, south, east, north, south, east

explanation.surface: Someone has a vague awareness of several points being made.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense is to perceive dimly; the letters also spell out a run of compass-point abbreviations.

clue.text: Scarf right out in river is mine

indicators.note: in places the shortened neckwear inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: out says a letter is removed from the neckwear word

parts.note: a cravat is a scarf worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A scarf found in the river is claimed by someone as theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes R from CRAVAT, leaving CAVAT, which goes 'in' EXE. 'mine' is the verb, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To mine is to dig out of the ground, the same as to excavate.

clue.text: Unusually prim lad with coin like anna

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters appear in an unusual order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strait-laced boy has a strange way with an Indian coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges PRIM LAD and COIN. An anna was an old Indian coin, which explains the surface; the definition reads the word as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Anna reads the same backwards as forwards, which is the property described.

clue.text: Opportunity for mounting Othello, for example

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the letters rise, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Othello, Shakespeare's tragic hero, is a Moor

explanation.surface: An actor has a chance to climb up into the role of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses MOOR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of scope or chance, as in room for improvement.

clue.text: Tempter taking in councillor is church officer

indicators.note: taking in says the devil's name swallows the other letters

parts.note: Satan is the Tempter in Christian tradition
taken as written

explanation.surface: The devil absorbs a local councillor who works for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' marks the container; 'is' is not a link here but part of what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan is the church officer in charge of the sacristy, its vestments and sacred vessels.

clue.text: Music-maker initially operating with subversive group

parts.note: a cell is a small group of subversives working within a larger body

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A musician starts working alongside an underground organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives O from 'operating', which follows CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a bowed string instrument, so it makes music.

clue.text: Incident in quiet retreat securing European's eternal bliss

indicators.note: in puts the incident inside the call for quiet

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
an event is an incident

indicators.note: securing means the retreat holds the European letter fast within it

parts.note: a haven is a safe retreat
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Something happens at a peaceful hideaway where a European finds endless joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'securing' each mark a container; 'Incident' looks like a noun of the surface but is the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the highest heaven of tradition, used for a state of supreme happiness.

clue.text: See evidence for successful defence

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references
an indication is a piece of evidence or a sign

explanation.surface: Look at the evidence presented for a winning case in court.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'vide' (see) is common in footnotes and crosswords alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindication is a clearing of someone's name, the outcome of a defence that succeeds.

clue.text: Separated but linked, like 21

definitions.meaning: describes two word parts kept apart yet joined by a short dash
the answer at 21 across is written with a dash between its two parts

explanation.surface: Two things are apart yet connected, as another entry is.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound joined by a short dash has its parts both divided and connected, like the cross-referenced two-part entry.

clue.text: Report of vessel in Irish river

indicators.note: report of means the clue word is heard rather than read, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: News comes of a boat seen on an Irish waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a pot, URN, whose sound gives the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erne flows through counties Cavan and Fermanagh in Ireland.

clue.text: Filial hatred? Ugly — out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are not in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's hatred of a parent is ugly and unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges HATRED and UGLY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Filial means relating to a son or daughter, so it fits behaviour proper to a female child.

clue.text: Great confusion about a certain source of fuel

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the other word
confusion says the letters of great are mixed up

parts.note: some, as in some person, means a certain one

explanation.surface: There is great confusion over a particular fuel supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' turns GREAT into GA...TER, which goes 'about' SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasholder stores town gas for supply, making it a source of fuel for homes.

clue.text: Awkward situation with advert? It can be stopped

parts.note: a plug is a bit of free publicity, an advert
to be in a hole is to be in an awkward situation

explanation.surface: An awkward moment involving an advertisement that ought to be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a sink's outlet is literally stopped with a bung.
explanation.definitionFit: A sink outlet is stopped by putting a rubber stopper in it.

clue.text: Cool manner of companion, one looking into complaint

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: looking into means the digit for one peers inside the word for a complaint

parts.note: an illness is a medical complaint
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A companion's cool bedside manner while examining an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking into' marks the container; Companion of Honour is a British order whose abbreviation crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilliness here is coldness of manner, an unfriendly reserve.

clue.text: Nurse in East Ham a hospital accommodates

indicators.note: accommodates says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A nurse working in East Ham is given a place by a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodates' signals the run inside 'Ham a hospital'. East Ham is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a nursemaid or maid in East and South Asia.

clue.text: Clothing ornament and ring found in ancient tower

indicators.note: found in says the ring shape sits inside the tower word

parts.note: a broch is an ancient round stone tower in Scotland
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery and a ring are dug up in a prehistoric tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts O inside BROCH, an Iron Age stone tower of northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch is an ornamental pin fastened to clothing.

clue.text: Like the special relationship entangling a lag in romance?

indicators.note: entangling says the following letters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A convict gets caught up in a love affair that raises a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangling' rearranges A LAG IN ROMANCE. The 'special relationship' is the phrase for close ties between Britain and the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The special relationship describes ties between Britain and the US, so it is of both nations.

clue.text: Gold lace Roman poet commonly mentioned

indicators.note: commonly mentioned means the name is said in a common accent that drops the H

parts.note: Horace was a Roman lyric poet

explanation.surface: A Roman poet often refers to golden trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Cockney accent the H is dropped, so the poet's name is said 'Orris.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a lace made of gold or silver thread, used to trim garments.

clue.text: Scented powder originally applied during sympathetic treatment

indicators.note: during places the letter in the middle of the treatment letters

parts.note: TLC stands for tender loving care

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A perfumed powder is first dabbed on during gentle care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives A from 'applied', which goes 'during' TLC.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder, often perfumed, is rubbed on the skin after a bath.

clue.text: Quixote's friend's bizarre 1 ac

indicators.note: bizarre says the letters take a strange new form, so rearrange them

parts.note: points to the answer at 1 across, the mature insect

explanation.surface: Don Quixote's companion is a very odd insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' rearranges the answer to 1 across. Quixote is Spanish, so his friend is Spanish too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a friend fits a companion of Cervantes's Spanish knight.

clue.text: Further considered in spite of being put in to soak

indicators.note: being put in says one piece is placed within the soaking verb

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it
though means in spite of the fact

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders despite being put in water to soak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put in' marks the container. Retting is soaking flax or hemp to loosen its fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: To rethink something is to consider it again, so it was considered further.

clue.text: Stone of enormous size shortly to be raised

indicators.note: to be raised means in this down entry the letters are read upwards
shortly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: mega means of enormous size

explanation.surface: A huge stone is soon to be lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims MEGA to MEG; 'to be raised' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem is a precious stone.

clue.text: One who acknowledges Edward, for example?.

definitions.meaning: someone who admits to a sin or crime
Edward, the English king canonised for his piety, bore this epithet

explanation.surface: Someone who owns up, perhaps a medieval king named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Confessor was an English king before the Norman Conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means someone who confesses, and is also the title of Edward the eleventh-century king.

clue.text: Went to ground without hesitation, being sticky

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the hiding word goes around

parts.note: to go to ground is to hide, so went to ground is hid
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone hid without pausing, and was sweaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so it marks a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Humid weather feels sticky with moisture in the air.
